**Feed**: dagen-med-di

**Market Sentiment**: Neutral

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

## Episode Thesis

Savings psychologist Niklas Laninge of Opti discusses the Swedish election parties' household-finance pledges: baby bonuses, higher child benefits and tax cuts. Citing research on US stimulus cheques and tax rebates, he argues that the form of a payout matters more than its size, and that such transfers do little for consumption or the economy. Vulnerable households mostly use the money to pay down debt. He also covers Invest America-style child savings accounts and the 15% of Swedish children with no savings. The episode has no equity-market view.
